params.body:
Ninety-one Eloquent models carried no `@property` annotations, so the analysis knew none of their
columns and wrote nine hundred findings about it. They are generated now, from the schema
(`ide-helper:models`), and that is what makes the analysis worth reading: from here on a typo in a
column name is caught instead of silently reading null.

**The harvest was smaller than that number suggests, and I would rather say so.** The annotations
surfaced fourteen new findings and not one of them was a bug:

- a tautology in a ternary in `ProcessImage` (the second branch re-tested what the first had already
  settled) — simplified, same behaviour;
- six `?->` on something that cannot be null — plain `->` now, which also says what the author knew;
- a pivot the analyser could not see from the other side of a `belongsToMany` — annotated on `Option`
  with the columns the relation carries.

All of them cleaned up here rather than written into the baseline, because a baseline that grows
when you look at it stops being a baseline:

| | |
|---|---|
| findings | 2.056 → **1.825** |
| entries | 76 removed, **0 added** (I diffed the two) |

**One generated line could not stand.** A column whose name begins with a digit
(`2ehandsbepremium_value`) cannot be a PHP property, so the generator wrote invalid PHPDoc that no
parser can read. A sentence in its place says where that column does live.

**What is left of that family is not about our models**, and it is worth naming so the next person
does not go looking: `auth()->user()` is an `Authenticatable` to the analyser (66 findings; this
Larastan has no setting to say otherwise), and the API resources reach their model through
`__get` (about a hundred). The second is the one to do next — a typo in a resource is a silent
null in what a partner receives, which is exactly the kind of thing nobody reports.

1.826 tests green.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
params.title: The models say which columns they have
